Judaism
/ˈdʒuː.deɪ.ɪ.zəm/
noun
From Greek Ioudaismos (Ἰουδαϊσμός) — the Jews’ religion/way of life (Galatians 1:13–14); from Judah / Judea. Covers the developing religion of the Jewish people from Second Temple streams through rabbinic, medieval, and modern forms (Orthodox, Conservative, Reform, etc.).

Biblical Definition

Judaism names the religious life and tradition of the Jewish people centered on the one God of Abraham, the Scriptures of Israel, and (in post-temple history) Torah, synagogue, and rabbinic teaching in place of the sacrificial system. In the New Testament era, “Judaism” and the varied Judaisms of the Second Temple world are the matrix from which the Messiah and the first church emerge. Jesus is the Jewish Messiah; the apostles are Jews; the Scriptures are Jewish; salvation is “from the Jews” (John 4:22). Christianity is not a Gentile invention bolted onto a discarded Bible — it is the fulfillment of Israel’s Scriptures in Jesus of Nazareth, crucified and risen. At the same time, post-apostolic Judaism that rejects Jesus as Messiah is not a second true gospel track (see Dual-Covenant Theology). Paul can speak of his former life “in Judaism” as zealous and yet needing Christ (Galatians 1:13–16; Philippians 3:4–8).

What it is: living tradition(s) of the Jewish people; historically essential context for Bible reading; object of Christian honor and gospel urgency.
What it is not: identical to “OT religion” frozen in amber; not a racial slur category; not proof that the church may despise Jews; not proof that Jews are saved without Christ.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828: JU'DAISM — the religious doctrines and rites of the Jews.

Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 6:4-5 — "Shema."

John 4:22 — "Salvation is from the Jews."

Romans 3:1-2 — "Advantage: oracles of God."

Romans 9:4-5 — "Privileges; Christ according to the flesh."

Galatians 1:13-14 — "Ioudaismos — Paul’s former life."

Acts 24:14 — "Paul worships the God of the fathers, believing all the Law and Prophets."

2 Corinthians 3:14-16 — "Veil in reading; turns to the Lord."

Modern Corruption

Caricature, romanticism, polemic laziness, and mission cowardice.

expand to see more

(1) Caricature — treating “the Jews” as a monolith or gospel villain set. (2) Romanticism — treating modern Judaism as automatically the pure OT faith without Messiah. (3) Polemic laziness — quoting “synagogue of Satan” texts without audience, covenant lawsuit context, or the full canonical restraint of Romans 11. (4) Mission cowardice — silence about Jesus out of social fear.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek Ioudaismos (Ἰουδαϊσμός); Judah / Judea.

expand to see more

G2454 Ἰουδαϊσμός (Ioudaismos) — the Jews’ religion / Jewish way of life (Gal 1:13–14).

Judah / Judea — tribal and geographic root of the ethnonym and the later religious label.
